articleTitle: The Airspace Capacity of Szolnok Airport
abstract: The aim of the article is to determine the airspace capacity of Szolnok Airport. The article focuses on the description of the airport's navigation equipment and the description of the procedures of the air traffic control service. The article publishes possible methods of guiding aircraft to Szolnok airport during radar vectoring using NDB, ILS, and PAR devices. The result is a 3D visualization of the airspace with a view to determining the capacity of the defined airspace.

articleTitle: Local Air Quality Studies for Supersonic Aircraft
abstract: The primary goal of SENECA (LTO noiSe and EmissioNs of supErsoniC Aircraft) project is to provide a basis for decision making of environmentally friendly supersonic aircraft design taken into account the detailed modelling of the emissions, the LTO noise and the local/global environmental impacts. One of the task of SENECA project to perform local air quality tasks for designed SST aircraft. Analysis of instantaneous calculated concentrations of CO and NOx for M1.8, B707 and Concord due to measurement campaign at DIA demonstrated the same trend as emission rates ratio of considered aircraft for taxi and take-off conditions. The concentration envelope of NOx (area of M1.8 airliner influence) is bounded by the 20 μg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with represents a small fraction of t hour standard of 200 μg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The area of influence ofM1.8 airliner for NOx (take-off and taxing conditions) is smaller than those predicted ones for Concord. The considered cases the areas of influence of B707, Concord and M1.8 airliner for take-off and taxi conditions are restricted to areas near the aircraft pathway, well within the airport boundaries.

articleTitle: Sustainable Innovation in 3D Printing: The Role of Thermoplastic Recycling
abstract: The boom in 3D printing has revolutionized manufacturing capabilities across all industries, offering unprecedented flexibility, adaptability and, last but not least, efficiency. However, the wide use of thermoplastic materials in the rapid prototyping process represents a significant environmental challenge due to the number of individual prototypes and the resulting accumulation of plastic waste. This article explores the potential of recycling thermoplastics in the industry as a means of promoting sustainable innovation. By integrating recycled thermoplastic materials into the production cycle, it is possible to reduce waste. The article deals with the possibilities of recycling thermoplastics and its influence on the mechanical properties of recycled thermoplastics. As the industry moves towards more sustainable manufacturing practices, the importance of recycled thermoplastics not only in the 3D printing industry will be key to creating a greener and more responsible future.

articleTitle: Engine installation effect contribution in noise performances of the new supersonic airplane
abstract: EU SENECA project considers two basic design configurations for new European supersonic airliner: the quad- engine and triple-engine – airframe integrated platforms, including their exploration and optimization for aircraft noise performances. Semi-empirical and ray acoustic modeling suggest that the noise installation effect will be influenced by sound reflection from the wing surface for fan inlet noise at certification points beneath the flight path, and by the twin- engine effect on jet noise at the sideline certification point. For triple-engine designs, the twin-engine effect may reduce jet noise by up to 3 EPNdB, while for quad-engine designs, this reduction could reach 5 EPNdB. Additionally, the wing's shielding effect could further reduce fan noise, potentially increasing overall noise reduction, but only if the engine nacelle is installed above the wing surface.

articleTitle: Implementation of medium and low precision IMUs for the design of integration architectures
abstract: The paper discusses in more detail some ways of modeling errors of inertial sensors and the way of testing the INS model case. Kalman filtering represents an important and sophisticated mathematical algorithm from the point of view of integration of navigation systems, which ensures the estimation of state variables. The implementation of this mathematical tool in program form requires the analysis of the dynamic system for which this filter is designed. In order to apply Kalman filtering, linearization is necessary, which, depending on the design, creates the possibility of applying a linearized KF or an extended KF estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of a Simple Aircraft Residual Current Device Control Logic
abstract: The paper presents a brief description of aircraft electrical protection devices, especially residual current devices (ground fault interrupters). The aim was to create a testbed for residual current device testing and current flow monitoring. Based on the results obtained from testbed, authors propose a simple control logic for residual current breaker in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment.

articleTitle: Boundary Layer Turbulence Identification in the Vicinity of Svidnik Airport
abstract: This article aims to provide information on the occurrence of turbulence in the atmospheric boundary layer as a hazardous weather phenomenon near Svidnik Airport. Flying in the traffic pattern and approaching for landing requires pilots to have heightened situational awareness, focus on piloting techniques, precise flight path planning, and proper maneuvering for landing. When turbulence is added to these factors, it can increase stress, especially for student pilots or pilots with limited experience landing at this airport. This article offers an overview of areas where turbulence occurs during traffic patterns, depending on the direction of the runway in use. These areas were identified based on a theoretical analysis of the terrain features around Svidnik Airport. Subsequently, these areas were practically identified through validation flights conducted by the co-author of this article as well as by students of the Faculty of Aeronautics in study program Pilot, who conduct educational flights from this airport.

articleTitle: Recent advances in hydrogen production for providing air transport needs
abstract: The paper presents critical analysis and current statistical data on recent advances in hydrogen production and supply for the use in aviation sector. The relevance of this research field is substantiated from the point of view of hydrogen potential to mitigate the aviation negative impact on climate. Currently available technologies for hydrogen production are presented and summarized as well as their potential to provide rising needs of industry. Statistical data on capacity of hydrogen production in Europe is provided with the special focus on hydrogen production by water electrolysis. Along with the paper considers forecast for hydrogen demand scenarios for hydrogen-powered aircraft for the period by 2050. The paper also considers current state and future challenges related to hydrogen supply and distribution within airport infrastructure.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Runway Area Division for More Accurate Pavement Condition Index Assessment
abstract: This article addresses the issue of designing a new layout of monitored areas for the implementation and evaluation of the Airport's Pavement Condition Index. Based on a comprehensive analysis of the life course of the reinforced cover at a specific airport, an evaluation of long-term operational characteristics, and the occurrence of defects, a new distribution of areas was proposed, which better reflects the operational load. Precisely targeted and effectively divided monitoring surfaces will enable better monitoring of the development of faults, evaluation and precisely targeted planning of funds for performing surface repairs. The airport operator will also be able to predict operating costs on precisely defined runway areas.

articleTitle: Evolution from Virtual Gaming into Mixed Reality Training
abstract: Mixed reality is being explored by leading air forces worldwide as a cutting-edge technology for pilot training simulations. To understand its potential, it’s important to look at the evolution of virtual reality (VR) and its limitations. VR creates fully artificial environments but lacks interaction with real-world objects, which is crucial for certain training applications. This limitation led to the development of mixed reality. Mixed reality merges augmented reality (AR) and VR, allowing physical and digital objects to coexist and interact in real-time. Leveraging affordable LCD displays and inertial measurement units (IMUs), played an important role in VR and MR development. After the initial wave the VR market became dominated by international corporations focused on gaming focused on rapid userbase acquisition led to significant investments in VR technology, advancing display technology. Industries like automotive, healthcare, and pilot training began adopting VR, showing a growing demand for high-resolution mixed reality (MR). In the simulation industry, visual acuity and fidelity are prioritized over cost, unlike the gaming industry where price and enjoyment are key drivers. Mixed reality is crucial for training military jet fighter pilots, who need to accurately perceive and identify objects and details for mission success and safety. Different training scenarios require varying levels of fidelity. Although the mobile phone industry facilitated the widespread adoption of modern virtual reality headsets and the gaming industry supported their development for several years, the recent decline in headset sales indicates that the pilot training market segment must now assume the responsibility for funding it further. This segment should establish clear objectives for the next generation of mixed reality devices, which are gaining increasing interest from experts, particularly when integrated with fully functional cockpit replicas.

articleTitle: Operational Assessment of the Remote Tower Concept
abstract: The remote tower is a current trend in air traffic management. Many providers of air navigation services in Europe and around the world are testing, implementing, or even already operating this concept. This paper focuses on the operational assessment of the Remote Tower concept in the context of Slovak international airports. The Slovak international airports of Piešt’any (LZPP), Poprad-Tatry (LZTT), and Žilina (LZZI) are airports with fewer movements and therefore also with low revenues. In the future, Remote Tower could be a solution for these airports by reducing investment and operating costs, increasing the quality of services provided, or extending opening hours. This article is devoted to the operational solution of control towers and their possible introduction at Slovak civil airports. The main goal of this paper is an operational assessment of the suitability of implementing remote tower technology at selected regional airports in Slovakia.

articleTitle: Safety on air transport in a multicultural working environment
abstract: This paper analyses the impact of cultural diversity on safety in the aviation sector. It identifies key human factors as well as safety procedures that play a crucial role in ensuring safe flight operations in a culturally diverse working environment. It does not focus on one selected element, but seeks to make visible the totality of the issues involved. Attention was drawn to the difficulty of identifying factors having a negative impact on teamwork. Conclusions and analysis of the problem addressed were based on a survey, conducted among employees of aviation companies. One of the main conclusions of the analysis indicates the need for periodic training of employees as well as the standardisation of language, also by eliminating dialects.

articleTitle: Recent Changes in European Aviation Legislation in Relation to the Training of Aeronautical Technical Personnel
abstract: The aviation industry is one of the most dynamic sectors, with safety and quality of service dependent on skilled aircraft maintenance personnel. European legislation, in particular Regulation (EC) No 2042/2003 and subsequently Regulation (EU) No 1321/2014, lays down the rules for maintenance and licensing of technicians. The Part-66 system defines licenses for different aircraft types, with B1 and B2 licenses being key. Continuous education and training of personnel is mandatory to ensure they are competent to work with new technologies. Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/989 introduced changes, including an increase in the number of test questions in each module. Certification of organizations providing Part-147 training is essential for safety and quality of instruction. The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the introduction of distance learning in the training of aviation technical personnel. In NATO, EMAR regulations, based on civilian standards, adapted to military conditions, are important for military personnel. In Slovakia, the TUKE Faculty of Aviation is a key entity integrating EMAR into the training of military technicians. Training of personnel according to EMAR ensures interoperability and a high level of quality in the maintenance of military aircraft.

articleTitle: Copernicus Satellite Data and Air Traffic Management
abstract: Using Copernicus, an Earth observation data collection system, in air traffic management introduces many possibilities. One of the goals of the Copernicus system is to make satellite data accessible to everyone. Therefore, it can be applied to aviation in several ways, such as monitoring airport infrastructure, tracking environmental changes, or enhancing security. By integrating this system, aviation operations can become more efficient and resilient. This article aims to examine the potential of this extensive data resource. The expected benefits of the research include improved airport safety and efficiency, as well as a reduction in environmental impacts.

articleTitle: Impact of continuous climb/descent procedure implementation on ATCO workload
abstract: As the density of air traffic increases, greater demands are being placed on its efficiency. Various initiatives within Air Traffic Management strive to optimize airspace design and corresponding procedures. Implementing continuous descent and climb operations has the potential to target capacity issues in high-density airspaces while optimizing flight operations to minimize impact on the environment. The underlying research seeks to prove that implementing procedures with vertical profiles positively affects air traffic controllers' workload and, thus, airspace capacity. The research results show that implementing vertical profiles in TMA improved air traffic control efficiency, which was reflected in both a reduction in the total communication time on the frequency and in the decreased number of tasks the controller has to conduct. Therefore, it can be concluded that procedures with vertical profiles can contribute to an efficient utilization of airspace.

articleTitle: The Use of UAVs in Assessing Damages to Onshore and Offshore Wind Power Stations
abstract: Wind power plants help protect the environment and have an increasing share in the world's energy mix. Recently, these machines have become larger and more powerful, but this constant growth also increases the risk to their surrounding areas in the event of malfunctions. These risks can be mitigated through regular inspections conducted by UAVs. Images captured by UAVs can be transformed into 3D models, which can be effectively used for maintenance purposes. UAV techniques, photogrammetry, and 3D modeling appear to be valuable tools for preventing environmental hazards.

articleTitle: Selection of Suitable Magnetic Microwires for Use in RTD Magnetometers Applicable on UAVs
abstract: Due to their dimensions, weight, and magnetic properties, magnetic microwires are suitable for use in Residence Time Difference (RTD) magnetometers. The choice of material composition for creating the microwire and the subsequent post-production processes significantly impact the quality of the microwire and, consequently, the quality of the signal obtained from the magnetometer. The aim of this paper is to summarize the results obtained from the experimental measurement of parameters for selected samples of glass-coated amorphous magnetic microwires with varying compositions and post-production processes. The results of the experimental measurements and their evaluation focus on the noise value of the entire measurement chain, the measurable range and the value of the switching field. The results from these experimental measurements will be used to select the most suitable types of magnetic microwires for the development of an RTD magnetometer with a microwire core.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of aircraft gas turbine engine failures caused by quality of fuel
abstract: The paper is devoted to the urgent problem raised in the Ukrainian Air Force and related to the reduction of reliability and durability of jet fighters in its fleet. The paper is focused on increased failures in the engines of Su-27 and MiG-29 fighters. The collection of real data and analysis of engine failures was done within the scope of this study. The detected failures were systematized according to the location of damage, its severity, and possible impact on the operability of the aircraft. This research is aimed at the analysis of characters and possible reasons for the detected damage appearance. The main focus of the study is engine damages and failures, which are caused by the quality of jet fuel used and the substantiation of fuel's negative impact on the reliability and operability of jet fighters. Received statistical data may be further used for the development of recommendations and practical measures for jet fuel supply to prevent and minimize engine damages, ensuring the reliability and airworthiness of military aircraft.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Software Support Analysis (SSA) in Civil Aircraft Life Cycle
abstract: The new generation of aircraft uses a large number of onboard software to realize system functions and interactions, which brings challenges to traditional aircraft development and operational support. In this paper, the SSA (Software Support Analysis) method is used to analyze the onboard software from the support view during the civil aircraft life cycle, including SSA candidates selection in the early stages, as well as the detailed analysis of various software support tasks. This research provides a set of solutions which enable the reasonable supportability of onboard software at all stages of the civil aircraft life cycle, as well as establishing the most cost-effective software support concept.

articleTitle: Examination of requirements and proposal of specifications for the educational simulator of tower air traffic control at the Faculty of Aeronautics
abstract: In the current era of increasing emphasis on safety and efficiency in air traffic, the importance of air traffic control is growing. This article focuses on designing and implementing a tower air traffic control simulator for the needs of the Faculty of Aeronautics at the Technical University of Košice. The work aims to provide students and future air traffic control professionals with practical skills and a deep understanding of flight control processes through a simulated environment that closely mimics real operations. The article analyzes current tower air traffic control simulators, their capabilities, and limitations, and based on the identified needs of faculty, proposes a suitable hardware and software solution for the simulator. This proposal for a simulator has the potential to significantly improve the quality of education and training for future ATC operators, thereby increasing the safety and efficiency of air traffic.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Life Cycle Assessment Tools for Aviation
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of various Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) tools for the use in the aviation industry. Given the significant environmental impacts associated with aviation, from the manufacture of aircraft to their operational lifecycle, it is crucial to leverage precise and robust LCA tools to guide sustainability initiatives. This study compares several prominent LCA tools including SimaPro, Shpera, Ecochain Mobius, Ecochain Helix, Umberto, OpenLCA, and GREET, based on criteria essential for effective environmental assessment. These criteria encompass the range of impact assessment methods, usability, the capability for generating detailed reports, sector-specific features, collaborative functionalities, and database comprehensiveness. The findings provide critical insights into each tool’s strengths and limitations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the CBA 3.0 Methodology in the Context of Determining Fuel Consumption for New Road Infrastructure
abstract: Efficient determination and expansion of transport capacity is now becoming crucial for the economic growth and efficient management of any business in the transport sector. The aim of investing in transport is to create beneficial social effects such as reducing transport costs, reducing travel times, eliminating accidents or other adverse environmental impacts of transport. By evaluating the specific steps of applying the CBA (Cost-Benefit Analysis) methodology to address fuel consumption in a company's transport infrastructure using a model project as an example, we can determine its role in determining an effective investment project solution. A comprehensive analysis of the CBA methodology and its implementation on a specific project, focusing on the calculation of fuel consumption using available data and traffic surveys, brought a new dimension of data analysis. Using the software, we investigated how the selected factors affect fuel consumption and the economic viability of the project. The comprehensiveness of conducting cost-benefit analyses served as a basis for decision making and investment decisions in accordance with the CBA methodology.

articleTitle: Multidisciplinary Design Optimization Framework for Morphing Wing using Metamaterials
abstract: Metamaterials introduce innovative possibilities for morphing wing design. This paper explores two methods of incorporating metamaterials into morphing wing design and applies a Multidisciplinary Design Optimization process to optimize and compare this design against a conventional composite wing. The analysis integrates aerodynamic, structural, and control considerations to evaluate the effectiveness of the metamaterial applications. The two approaches involve a variable-stiffness leading edge surface, and a trailing edge equipped with a metamaterial lattice hinge for smooth deformation. The paper presents the Multidisciplinary Design Optimization framework and initial findings from individual analyses, linking two-dimensional aero-structural wing rib design with surrogate models that extend to three-dimensional aerodynamic and control evaluations.

articleTitle: Measuring the Company's Efficiency Using the DEA Method
abstract: In the modern era of air transport, characterized by dynamic growth and constant change, efficiency and competitiveness are crucial for airlines. Airlines need to constantly evaluate and monitor their efficiency, especially in a world where environmental pressures, technological advances and changing passenger preferences create new challenges. The article points out the possibilities of using DEA (Data Envelopment Analysis) method to measure the efficiency of a selected airline company. After selecting a suitable mathematical model, we created a dataset on the basis of which we carried out the measurement and evaluation of efficiency with the help of the DEAFrontier add-on software of Microsoft Excel. We conclude that some indicators affect efficiency more than others and that there is a situation where the airline itself does not have to account for inefficient operations, as the period of the global Covid-19 pandemic illustrates. The DEA method represents a useful way to measure airline efficiency, its flexibility offers the ability to adapt to different areas and aspects. Furthermore, it can appropriately identify the procedures for the most efficient direction of companies' activities.

articleTitle: Impact analysis and benefits of airspace modernization
abstract: The article provides an analysis of the issue of the modernization of airspace and presents the benefits that modernization brings. The aim of this article is to examine and analyze the benefits that arise from the modernization of airspace. In order to elaborate the issue and fulfil the objectives, analytical research was carried out, which consisted of data analysis and studies related to this issue. Based on the knowledge and results obtained, it is possible to present a detailed view of the benefits that the modernization of European airspace brings. In this way, the paper seeks to contribute to a better understanding of the benefits associated with the modernization of airspace.

articleTitle: Hybrid Technology for Assessing the Fatigue Level of Air Traffic Controllers Using Video Surveillance
abstract: The article presents the research results on developing a hybrid technology for assessing air traffic controller fatigue using video surveillance and expert opinion. The technology makes it possible to obtain quantitative and linguistic levels of fatigue of air traffic controllers to signal to the manager to make proactive decisions to improve air traffic safety. The hybrid technology consists of three successive stages, which have their acceptable levels, namely: assessment of fatigue of air traffic controllers based on video surveillance and specialized software; expert evaluation of the level of fatigue of air traffic controllers; a hybrid technology that combines video surveillance data and expert judgment to derive a comprehensive linguistic level of fatigue for air traffic controllers. The hybrid technology was verified and configured on the real data of the work of air traffic controllers, where the participants were students of the Faculty of Aeronautics of the Technical University of Košice.

articleTitle: ICAO Standards for Language Skills and Current Language Ability of Students of Aeronautical Faculty
abstract: The introductory part of the article deals with the issue of licensing of aviation personnel in general. It explains the meaning and content of the basic international legal standards for the licensing of aviation specialists at the global level, but also at the level of the European Union countries. It highlights the importance of the linguistic competence required for the licensing of aviation professionals. After the theoretical part, the article presents the main research tasks carried out in recent years in the field of language training and their results. The research was carried out with students of the Faculty of Aeronautics of the Technical University in Košice, as well as with experts from aviation practice. Based on the relevant results, potential possibilities of implementation in the conditions of the Faculty of Aeronautics of the Technical University of Košice are proposed. The most significant disadvantages of each of them are presented for both options and for the potentially more advantageous option the possible way of its practical implementation is also presented.

articleTitle: Risk management of increased workload of air traffic controllers
abstract: The article deals with the risk management of the increased workload of air traffic controllers. Brainstorming methods, expert estimates and event tree analysis were used. Using the mentioned methods, 6 hazards and the resulting 11 risks were identified, which were assessed according to the security risk assessment matrix. One of the identified risks was assessed as unacceptable and 7 risks were assessed as tolerable. One unacceptable risk and a high number of tolerable risks indicate the necessary need to take corrective measures and to take a proactive approach to risk reduction.The conclusion of this work and risk analysis further shows that despite extremely unlikely risks such as a collision between aircraft, it is important to consider and address less serious but more likely risks such as insufficient coordination between controllers and pilots or reduced attention and concentration. Using standard aviation phraseology is key to minimizing misunderstandings, but it's also important to implement stress management and wellness programs to reduce the risk of failure to respond to changing situations. ATCos workload regulation is also essential to maintain optimal levels of performance and attention, especially in high-traffic environments. Last but not least, it is important to train ATCos in response to emergency situations and emphasize the importance of quick and effective communication and decision-making.

articleTitle: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence in Civil Aviation
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the aviation industry is revolutionizing operational efficiency, safety, and the passenger experience. This paper provides a comprehensive examination of the current and potential applications of AI in aviation. The introduction defines AI and outlines its key characteristics, setting the stage for a detailed exploration of its practical uses. The second chapter reviews case studies of airlines that have successfully implemented AI technologies, highlighting improvements in areas such as flight operations, customer service, and scheduling. The third chapter focuses on future applications, particularly predictive maintenance, and its potential to enhance reliability and reduce costs. The final chapter presents a SWOT analysis, assessing the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats associated with the adoption of AI in aviation. By synthesizing these elements, the paper aims to provide insights into how AI can shape the future of the industry and inform strategic decision-making..

articleTitle: Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Airside Vehicles Business Models
abstract: The adoption of electric autonomous vehicles (EAVs) is set to revolutionize airport ground operations. Airports are increasingly developing new autonomous innovation strategies to meet sustainability goals and address future challenges, such as shifting labor markets, evolving working conditions, and the growing impact of digitalization [1]. The traditional business model, in which manufacturers sell vehicles to operators (ground handlers), may no longer be relevant. The increasing complexity and advancement of EAVs will drive up costs, making the ownership model less appealing and shifting the focus from product-oriented to service-oriented models. This paper aims to provide a conceptual framework for potential business models for the implementation of EAVs in airport airside operations.

articleTitle: Modern Avionics and ATM Technologies Implementation Gap Analysis Latvian and Georgian Case Studies
abstract: According to Eurocontrol’s latest research, by year 2035 airports across Europe are expected to handle 14.4 million flights and 1.4 billion passengers. However, current Air Traffic Management (ATM) system is not adequately prepared for such volume of air traffic, and as a result it might lead to a congested airspace, causing even more delays on ground and in the air. This situation is economically inefficient and has a significant adverse impact on environment due to carbon emission and noise pollution. For this reason, continuous development and modernization of the ATM system is necessary. The Global Air Navigation Plan (GANP) is a flexible engineering-technical methodological document that allows all International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) member states to advance their air navigation capacities based on their specific operational requirements. One of the most problematic parts for successful implementation of the GANP is an innovative ATM, modern avionics technologies and effective interrelation between systems and users, considering ergonomic factors. A system "operator-machine-environment" depends on human performance, as well as on a level of automation of systems involved. Paper focuses on Latvian and Georgian case studies, as in both counties ATM technologies and level of automation continuously grows and becomes more advanced. The development of modern aircraft avionics systems requires new skills of aviation professionals that is why training becomes even more challenging and important. As a result of the research a methodological approach and general model for effective interconnection of modern avionics and innovative ATM technologies is proposed, taking into consideration human factors.

articleTitle: The Proposal for Eliminating the Most Common Causes of Air Accidents in Czechia and Slovakia
abstract: This paper presents a thorough analysis of the most common causes of air accidents in Czechia and Slovakia in the time period 2018-2022 and comparing these findings with international data to identify effective preventive measures. The study also explores the implementation of global safety plans, specifically those related to air accidents, and emphasizes the importance of national safety strategies such as SPAS, which is already in place in Czechia. It highlights the need for Slovakia to develop a similar strategic safety document. The analysis reveals that the causes of air accidents can be systematically categorized and emphasizes that avoiding the repetition of past mistakes is crucial in civil aviation. This necessitates changes in legislation at both international and national levels, which have already led to modifications in training programs. The paper assesses the effectiveness of recent updates to pilot training programs, particularly the 100 KSA and AUPRT, which aim to enhance pilots' ability to handle unusual or stressful situations and prevent loss of aircraft control. The conclusions underscore the importance of tailoring safety strategies to local conditions to enhance aviation safety. The primary objective of this paper was to develop a draft aviation safety plan for Slovakia that aligns with both regional and global safety standards.

articleTitle: Design Proposal of Landing and Lighting Systems for Svidnik Airport
abstract: The aim of this paper is to design landing and lighting systems for Svidnik Airport based on an analysis of current approach procedures, the technical equipment used at airports, and the geographical, topographical, and technical characteristics of the airport and its surroundings. The analysis of Svidnik Airport is carried out using UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) technology and maps from the Geodetic Survey of the Slovak Republic. The airport’s topography and geographical location are assessed. In the practical section, a landing system is proposed, along with an evaluation of the selected approach procedure’s applicability and the system’s usability. Additionally, the airport’s runway and taxiway lighting systems, a simple approach lighting system, and the PAPI (Precision Approach Path Indicator) system are proposed. The design of the lighting systems results in simple sketches that meet regulatory requirements and are applicable to Svidnik Airport.

articleTitle: Aviophobia Among Young Commuters: Rational Concerns or Emotional Response?
abstract: Fear of flying, or aviophobia, is a significant issue affecting a substantial portion of the population, with young adults being particularly vulnerable. Despite the high safety record of aviation, this irrational fear can severely impact an individual’s willingness or ability to travel by air, especially in the context of increasing global air traffic. This study investigates the factors contributing to fear of flying among young commuters aged 18-26 using a stated preference survey. The analysis highlights that fear is primarily driven by emotional responses to situational triggers rather than rational assessments of air travel safety. Key predictors of fear include concerns about terrorism, aviation accidents, and adverse weather conditions, with these factors exerting significant emotional influence despite their statistical rarity. The study also reveals a disconnect between objective safety perceptions and subjective fear, indicating that even passengers who acknowledge the general safety of air travel may still experience anxiety triggered by situational factors.

articleTitle: Simulation Model of Logistics Processes for Baggage Handling at Airports
abstract: Simulation modelling of logistics processes in baggage handling at airports is an important tool for optimising and streamlining processes within air transport. Airport logistics systems must cope with the ever-increasing number of passengers and baggage, emphasizing safety, reliability and speed. The baggage handling process can be analysed and optimised using simulation models, from handover, sorting, and transportation to delivery to the aircraft or baggage belt upon arrival. These models make it possible to identify bottlenecks in the process, test different scenarios, and design solutions that improve the fluidity and capacity of the system. This paper aims to optimize and streamline airport baggage handling logistics processes using simulation modeling, focusing on improving safety, reliability, and efficiency. The baggage handling process is considered from transfer and sorting to transportation and loading using Discrete Event Simulation (DES) and Agent Based Modeling (ABM). This allows us to test different scenarios and identify bottlenecks in the process. These methods provide a realistic representation of the ever-changing dynamics of airport operations, which increases resource efficiency, reduces costs, and improves customer satisfaction. To ensure that departure schedules are met and save human costs, the simulation tool allows for the best allocation of manpower based on the number of baggage items, arrival times, and processing system data.

articleTitle: Innovative software tool for cyber security against security incidents in civil aviation network operations
abstract: The Security Incident and Operation Centre is designed to aggregate events from heterogeneous systems, analyze them, and alert any deviations from expected behavior. It was developed for the "Innovative software tool for cyber security against security incidents in civil aviation network operations" project to gather and analyze security events from object and network security and monitoring systems. Aim of this paper is to introduce the system, explain how it works, its shortcomings and real-life experience upon which the system was periodically improved. After analyzing the use and the results we discuss the shortcomings and the ability of the system to fight these mistakes as well as giving tools to the users to fix them on the go, which adds to the system usability and versatility. In the end we conclude that the system does achieve its set goals.

articleTitle: Perspective methods for high performance Cubesat attitude control
abstract: This paper presents the overview of attitude control challenges for Cubesat missions with stringent pointing requirements and operational constraints. Survey of recent Cubesat attitude control applications is provided, followed by introduction of typical models needed for Cubesat attitude control problem formulation. Robustness to parametric uncertainty, disturbance rejection, constraints handling, and computational effort are the main identified control challenges. Three control design approaches, robust pole placement, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> design, and model predictive control are discussed with respect to the main challenges. Along with a traditional controller, each controller ability to cope with the given challenge is evaluated. Future research direction of attitude control formulation for two primary spacecraft operational modes, precise attitude tracking and attitude maneuvering, is justified.

articleTitle: Runway-Slope Illusions: A Systematic Review and Experimental Insights with Implications for Future Research
abstract: Runway slope illusions, a significant challenge in aviation, can distort pilots’ perception during critical phases of flight, particularly approach and landing. This study explores the susceptibility of pilots to these illusions in a controlled simulator environment using virtual reality technology. A systematic review of existing literature was conducted using the PRISMA methodology, revealing a notable gap in experimental studies directly addressing runway slope illusions. Subsequently, an experimental investigation was designed where 15 pilots performed repeated approaches to runways with varying slopes. Key performance metrics such as mean deviation from the ideal glide slope, standard deviation, RMSE, and time spent below the glide slope were analyzed. Although no statistically significant differences were found across the different runway slopes, patterns emerged, highlighting performance variability, especially on upslope runways. The findings underscore the need for further research into the effects of runway slope illusions on pilot performance, particularly under varying flight conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of the airspace overload and performance of air traffic control over the Europe
abstract: The aviation industry faced the greatest challenges in the last years. The devastating consequences of COVID-19 and the war situation in Ukraine have strongly affected the aviation market. Recovery of the volumes was expected during the year 2024 and a total surpasses of volumes in the year 2025. Still, several airliners called for immediate actions of authorities to European ATC's underperformance which caused several delays and cancellations during the summer of 2024. This article aims to assess the evolution of the capacity of the European air traffic management system. The related research was carried out using the data analysis method. The main goal of the research was to analyze the actual status of the air traffic management system related to airspace overload and to emphasize the need for the implementation of measures that can improve the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Bridging the Skies: analyzing Unmanned Traffic Management from a defense-centric perspective
abstract: The proliferation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), presents a novel challenge for the aviation industry, particularly for air traffic control, which ensures safe, orderly, and expeditious flow within its area of responsibility. In order to safeguard conventional traffic, it is imperative to establish a new operational environment that calculate with UAS flights, highlighting the critical nature of managing the coexistence of manned and unmanned aircraft. This led to the development of the Unmanned Traffic Management framework, typically addressing relatively small and mainly civilian drone’s operations at lower altitudes. However, it is crucial to define the scope and challenges of such a system from a defense-centric perspective, therefore this study outlines the necessary services and functions related to the operation of UTM systems. Examining the military’s multifaceted role of encompassing service provision, airspace utilization, airport operations, regulatory oversight, and cybersecurity aspects enables to unleash the full-scale of potential benefits of Unmanned Traffic Management. This publication argues that by leveraging advanced technological and regulatory frameworks, the defense-centric perspective can lead to the safe, secure, and efficient integration of drones into the national airspace structure. Actionable insights and strategic recommendations, fostering a resilient and collaborative UTM ecosystem is also introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Development of Military Pilot Competencies During Studies at the University of Defence
abstract: This study focuses on monitoring the development of military pilots' competencies during their studies at the University of Defence. It uses an innovative approach involving comprehensive testing of applicants and periodic assessment of students using flight simulators. The research combines analysis of performance in simulator exercises and real flight training. Results show a moderate correlation between performance in simulator exercises and real flight training, supporting the use of these methods to prepare future military pilots effectively. The study also reveals specific areas where students show the most progress or difficulty during training, providing valuable information for potential curriculum modifications.
